definition: Fervent means burning with intense feeling — belief, hope, or devotion that keeps its heat.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word fervent. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know fervent should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The bakery's regulars are fervent defenders of the Tuesday rye — question it and see what happens.
Wholehearted commitment is complete and sincere, but it is calmer than fervent — all of the heart, none of the fever.
Fanatical goes further than fervent — fervent devotion still listens to reason; fanatical devotion has hung up the phone.

Passionate is the everyday word for strong feeling of any kind — you can be passionate about soccer, a person, or pizza. Fervent is narrower and hotter: it belongs to belief, hope, prayer, and devotion, feeling that burns steadily. A passionate fan yells for a night; a fervent believer keeps the flame lit for years.

Heartfelt means deeply and sincerely meant — warmth without the blaze. Fervent takes the same sincerity and sets it alight: fervent hope burns, while heartfelt thanks simply glow. When feeling is genuine but calm, heartfelt is the right word; fervent requires heat.

Nine years later she still opens the garage at six, checks the tires herself, and plans the route around whichever block has the fewest library cards.
